items.summary: Implement backend data models and APIs for a live name-list checker: admin can upload/manage a list of names; users can claim a name; the system must prevent duplicate claims and track claim status (available/pending/approved/rejected) along with claimant identifier, timestamp, and UPI ID collected at claim time.

Add backend support for admin-configurable limits and totals: admin can set claim limits (e.g., maximum number of pending/approved claims overall and/or per user) and a per-claim rate/amount; backend must compute and expose totals based on claims (at minimum totals for approved claims, and optionally pending totals) and enforce limits during claim creation.
Add backend support for admin-managed public contact information, including a WhatsApp number, that can be updated in the admin panel and queried by the user view.

Create/extend frontend React Query hooks (in the existing hooks pattern used by frontend/src/hooks/useQueries.ts) for: uploading/replacing the name list, fetching the list, creating a claim with UPI ID, fetching claim status for a name, fetching admin claim queues, approving/rejecting claims, fetching totals, and getting/setting contact info and limits.

Add a user-facing ‘Live List Checker’ UI flow that allows a user to: view instructions, enter a name, see availability, and if available submit a claim by entering their UPI ID; the UI must show clear feedback when a name is already taken and show the user the status of their submitted claim (at least pending/approved/rejected).

Extend the existing Admin Panel (frontend/src/pages/AdminPanel.tsx) with a new section/tab for the Live List Checker that supports: uploading/replacing the name list (bulk text input and/or file upload), viewing all claims, filtering by status, approving/rejecting claims, setting limits and per-claim amount, viewing totals, and editing contact info including WhatsApp number.

Add required backend state upgrade handling for the new live list checker storage (name list, claims, settings/limits, contact info) using backend/migration.mo according to the project’s conditional migration policy, ensuring existing stored data (current comment lists, images, messages, etc.) is preserved.

Apply a coherent visual theme for the new Live List Checker pages/sections that matches the existing app’s Tailwind/Shadcn styling but is distinct and consistent (e.g., ‘warm amber + charcoal’ with card-based layout, clear status badges, and accessible form states). Do not use a blue/purple primary theme.
